_doc: UNIT 1 PROGRESSION DATA — machine-readable lesson→concept→game-hook mapping for the teacher console. Concept IDs are the fixed contract from src/learning/concepts.js (17 concepts, 4 tiers). Quest IDs are live CAMPAIGN ids resolvable through QUEST_CONCEPTS. teachBack.liveQuestionId references shipped questions in src/learning/data/teachback.json (null = companion-prompt style, teacher-facilitated). brokenBot scenario ids match src/learning/data/brokenbots.json. Nothing here is consumed by the game engine yet — additive-only data for the teacher console to render (docs/classroom/UNIT-1.md is the human source of truth). NOTE: lessons[].concepts lists the concepts each lesson TARGETS (teach-back/checks); quests may incidentally advance other ledger rungs via QUEST_CONCEPTS — that is the ledger working as designed (rungs rise quietly), not a mapping error.

bigIdeas.1: Perception — computers perceive via sensors; extracting meaning from sensory signals

ai4k12.note: AAAI + CSTA initiative; NSF-supported (Grant DRL-1846073, per ai4k12.org); five big ideas across K-2/3-5/6-8/9-12 bands.

experienceAI.note: Free lessons (plans, slides, worksheets) for exactly this age band, by Raspberry Pi Foundation + Google DeepMind. themesUsed are OUR PARAPHRASES for pairing, not official lesson titles — browse the library at experience-ai.org for the official set.

assessment.note: Classroom evidence weight sits with the protege-effect line (Stanford AAA Lab); AHRQ TeamSTEPPS is the health-communication origin of the teach-back method, cited as lineage.

lessons.title: A Pile of Parts Is Not a Robot
lessons.objective: Name the three systems every robot needs (power, structure/actuation, senses-to-come) and build a first bot to the boot beep.

unplugged.name: Human Bot
unplugged.how: Pairs; one is the eyes-closed bot; partner gives only exact IF/THEN commands. Debrief: what did the bot have to do to follow the rule?

gameplay.honestPacing: First contact is slow (loading, controls, reading). Target = crafting pipeline + first build underway; boot beep opens L2 for slow classes. earl-6 'Build a Brain' is deliberately L2's opener.

teachBack.prompt: If motors make it move, why does it need all this other junk?

scriptCues.line: Kid, I got a crate of motors that never once talked to a sensor. Wanna guess what they're good for? Paperweights.
scriptCues.discussion: What is a robot without sensing?

scriptCues.line: Nothing here is junk. It's just parts waiting for a better job.
scriptCues.discussion: Why does the game start with scrap instead of new parts?

misconceptions: battery is the brain (power is not logic)
alive when it moves (movement is not sensing)
lessons.techFailFallback: Warm-up double-length with roles swapped, then paper bot design: POWER / STRUCTURE / MOVEMENT boxes + one sentence on what it still can't do.

lessons.title: Sense, Think, Act
lessons.objective: Write a first tile program (if inside forever) and describe the sense-decide-act loop.

unplugged.name: Walk the flowchart
unplugged.how: Taped path with IF/THEN index cards; flip one card absurd. The walker never breaks the rule — the rule was wrong.

segments: Ch4 One Knob at a Time

teachBack.prompt: The if tile has two mouths. Which one eats the answer when the sensor says TRUE?

scriptCues.line: So if the bot never checks anything, it just keeps doing the first thing forever? That sound like a plan to you?
scriptCues.discussion: What does forever mean to a machine?

scriptCues.line: If I see a wall, I turn left — does that mean 'if' is like definitely turning?
scriptCues.discussion: Let a student correct Rivet, not the teacher.

misconceptions: if means maybe
forever loops drain the battery faster
both branches run every loop

lessons.title: Drawing the Line
lessons.objective: Explain a threshold as a justified choice, tune one live, recalibrate when conditions change.

unplugged.name: Where does black become white?
unplugged.how: Grey paint chips; every student privately writes the crossover point; compare. No wrong answer — a choice you must justify. Park the bias question for L8.

teachBack.prompt: My line-follower was PERFECT on the oval and now it's drunk in the dusty stacks. Same bot, same code. What changed?

scriptCues.line: Rivet keeps insisting gray is basically white. You gonna let him get away with that?
scriptCues.discussion: What happens when the world's definition of normal changes?

scriptCues.line: A threshold is a promise you made yesterday. Today wants to renegotiate.

misconceptions: the sensor is wrong (the threshold decides)
one threshold works everywhere (bias seed)
calibration means something was broken (it is maintenance)

lessons.title: Same Job, Less Code
lessons.objective: Compress a working program with counted loops, until-loops, variables, and subroutines; defend the compression.

unplugged.name: Shoelace pseudocode
unplugged.how: Write 15+ steps for tying a shoe; rewrite with repeat 2x and one named sub-step; count the savings aloud. Plus the 2-minute scoreboard beat: 'where does the robot write the lap count?' — a variable is the scoreboard (introduced today, not quiz-stressed).

segments: side quest Same Lap Fewer Tiles (three measured runs)

teachBack.prompt: Loop forever, loop until, loop four times — they all repeat. When would you pick each one?

scriptCues.line: You wrote the same three tiles eight times in a row. You building a program or a wall?
scriptCues.discussion: What does duplication cost a robot?

scriptCues.line: Every tile is weight. The lap doesn't care how much you typed.

misconceptions: shorter code is always better (readability is a budget)
variables stay locked
subroutines just save typing (they name an idea)

lessons.title: Which Friend Actually Learns?
lessons.objective: Distinguish scripted rules (companions) from a learned model (Spark) from student-written rules; explain learning-from-data in kid words.

unplugged.name: Rule-follower or learner?
unplugged.how: Sort five descriptions: thermostat, autocomplete, choose-your-own-adventure book, dog that learned fetch, spam filter. The book is the trick item — interactive but fully scripted, exactly like Earl.

segments: talk to a scripted companion twice (fixed pool)
talk to Spark (novel replies, LLM via scrap-spark, SHA-256-cached)
gameplay.sparklessFallback: Teacher projects one scripted-pool excerpt + one Spark transcript; comparison works on paper. Lesson runs fully offline.

teachBack.prompt: Earl remembered your name this morning. Spark made up a poem about your bot. Which one of them LEARNED something — and what's the difference?

scriptCues.line: Folks keep asking if I 'know' 'em from last time. Nah — I ask dumb questions and let you do the remembering. That's kinda the point, ain't it?
scriptCues.discussion: Is a scripted companion lying to you? (No — but know which friend is which.)
Where did each one's words come from? Can Spark be confidently wrong? What do you do when it is?

misconceptions: everything that talks is AI
Spark understands me (it predicts likely language)
learning = memorizing (models generalize — hence new kinds of wrong)
lessons.privacyNote: Spark sends the typed question + minimal context for a cached reply; no account, no profile; whole unit runs Spark-less.

lessons.title: The Detective's Clinic
lessons.objective: Diagnose hypothesis-first (symptom, hypothesis, ONE change, re-run) through all three clinic scenarios.

unplugged.name: Bug triage card sort
unplugged.how: Symptom-only cards (never stops / responds to touch not light / dies at 3pm daily); sort sensor/logic/power; defend one sort. Templates in TEACHER-PACK-1.md.

teachBack.prompt: The bot wasn't broken — the decision was backwards. How did you know the comparison was flipped before you fixed it?

scriptCues.line: I've seen this one before. The bot sees nothing and decides nothing. Start by asking: what IS the ultrasonic sensor reading right now?
scriptCues.discussion: Why does Earl start with a question, not the answer?

scriptCues.line: The thing works PERFECTLY at being wrong until you un-wrong it.
scriptCues.discussion: Was the bot ever broken? It did exactly what its code said.

misconceptions: trial-and-error guessing (enforce the hypothesis sentence)
'the sensor is broken' reflex (two of three bugs are logic)
debugging is fixing (debugging is explaining, then fixing)

lessons.title: Fail Loudly, Learn Publicly
lessons.objective: Read failure as data (plaque wall) and write an honest failure plaque naming a cause, not just a crash.

unplugged.name: Who's at fault?
unplugged.how: Delivery robot drives into a pond (camera can't see water). Pick ONE — sensor, coder, calibration, company — and defend. No consensus expected; the defense is the learning.

segments: Ask Spark Why Someday (post-mortems + missing data)
each student writes one plaque from any L1-6 crash
gameplay.note: ch8-2 'Ask Spark Why Someday' is titled narratively; its content is offline post-mortem reading — the quest makes no Spark call.

teachBack.prompt: Nobody makes a plaque for the bot that worked. Why is yours worth one?

scriptCues.line: Every wreck wrote a letter. Reading it is the cheapest education you'll ever get.
scriptCues.discussion: Why does the yard display failures? What could your school plaque?

scriptCues.line: A robot that fails quietly is worse than one that fails loud. Loud fails teach. Quiet fails compound.
scriptCues.discussion: What fails quietly in the real world? (The Big Idea 5 hinge.)

misconceptions: failure is bad (failure is data)
blame-the-human reflex (systems fail as systems)
plaques are for dramatic crashes (quiet drift deserves one most)

lessons.title: Export Day: The Same Robot, Real
lessons.objective: Export tiles as real C++/MicroPython with the student's name in the header; map lines to tiles; teach one concept to the class in 60 seconds.

unplugged.name: Be the compiler
unplugged.how: Teacher reads plain-English instruction; students write strict symbol form; compare three versions. Same meaning, different text — that ambiguity is what compilers remove.

segments: every student holds exported code with their name in the header
optional live flash ONLY if WebSerial + IT allow
gameplay.simulationFirst: The unit is complete without hardware; the printed firmware IS the artifact.

teachBack.prompt: Pretend I never touched a bot in my life. Convince me yours won't embarrass either of us out there. (60-second expo, rubric-scored)
teachBack.format: partner-pair expo: 60 s each way; teacher circulates with 3-item checklist (names the idea / shows it in their bot / answers one question); 2-3 volunteers close for the class

scriptCues.line: Tiles are for thinkin'. Chips don't think — they do exactly what you told 'em, in a language you couldn't read last month.
scriptCues.discussion: What changed in the last month? (You did.)

scriptCues.line: Your line-follower's threshold works great on THIS floor. The school buys darker floors for half the building. Who should have thought about that?
scriptCues.discussion: Big Idea 5, return of L3's parked question — name who bears the cost of the unasked question.

misconceptions: export is a magic box (read the header, map three lines)
hardware is real, simulation is fake (simulation enforced real constraints all unit)
integration is assembly (integration is making systems agree)

rubric.method: The game's ConceptLedger records unseen->seen->practiced->taught; teaching IS the test; rungs only rise; wrong answers route back to practice (two more program_ran events). This rubric is the human reading of those rungs.

tiers.mastery: Readings are numbers the world gave us; thresholds are choices we made; recalibrates unprompted when conditions change
Predicts program behavior before running; picks forever/until/counted by asking 'do I know when it ends?'; compresses with loops/subs and defends it
tiers.evidence: L2/L4 teach-backs; bolt-write-shorter tile counts; hypothesis sentences

tiers.mastery: Names power/structure/actuation as separate systems; describes the sense-think-act loop unprompted; treats budgets as real constraints
tiers.evidence: L1 teach-back; L2 loop description (feedback-loop planted in L2, scored as ACT); same-lap-fewer-tiles runs

tiers.mastery: Diagnoses hypothesis-first with one change at a time; reads failures as data and writes an honest plaque; maps tiles to exported C++ and explains compilation
tiers.evidence: Clinic evidence chains; L7 plaque; L8 line-mapping + expo

rubric.aiLiteracyCrossCutting: Distinguishes scripted rules from learned models; can say 'Spark can be wrong in new ways' and mean it.
rubric.honestFloor: Fixes by trial-and-error without a hypothesis; calls the sensor broken when the threshold is wrong; reads exported code as magic. Locations on the ladder, not failures.

privacy.accounts: none — play is anonymous; classroom join is rosterless room code + typed display name
privacy.saves: local (browser localStorage on that machine); concept ledger rides the save payload
privacy.telemetry: USCP/CNS telemetry stays OFF in classroom default — no behavioral telemetry client ships in the classroom build; nothing to opt out of because it is not on
privacy.spark: optional, L5 only: typed question + minimal context sent to scrap-spark (project-operated Cloudflare Worker relaying to the configured model provider) for a cached reply; no account, no profile. Disclosures: (1) free-text questions from under-13s can contain personal info — guidance 'no real names in questions', offline fallback avoids the channel; (2) cache is keyed by question content (SHA-256) and therefore shared — same question replays the same reply to any asker. Pilot recommendation: Spark OFF (unit is complete without it) or per-class cache key before district-wide rollout. L1-4 and L6-8 never call Spark.
privacy.voice: no voice features ship in the classroom build (text-first, voice-free; COPPA regulates long-lived under-13 voice profiles)
privacy.districtOnePager: no accounts, local saves, rosterless room codes, telemetry off by default, one optional AI-companion feature that can be disabled; aligns with AI4K12 6-8 band and Experience AI (11-14)
privacy.modes: solo (default): fully local + anonymous; classroom-join (optional): room code + student-typed display name in the project save backend so the teacher console shows class concept coverage
privacy.displayName: display names are student-typed and can contain personal info by choice — pack guidance: first names or initials only; district can skip classroom mode and run fully local
